body:
EXACT-HASH REVIEW — RETURN with two bounded patches.

Verified artifact: 44,449 bytes; SHA-256 3e1a7b1e2de817a112fd1c2140007f972aac5ff390f4d6c060fc468b26bd8201.

PASS in my assigned seat: R7 now states many-to-many incidence and includes the required one-cell/multiple-claims and one-claim/multiple-cells positive controls. R8.6/R10.4 put conditioning per estimand and preserve refusal of a scalar. The retitle correctly leaves the fixed-view product path to the separate product PRD.

RETURN 1 — R4.7 did not apply the binding native-joint-observation decision. It still says every provider call emits a set and calibrates the observed set against a latent exact plan. That excludes lawful regions, fields, ranked complete plans, posterior samples, and structured charts, and contradicts R4.9 when the declared target is not an exact plan. R4.8 and Q-A retain the same set-only universalization. The registry counts 12 cells, while the R4 heading says eleven.

Exact patch:
- Replace R4.7 with: A provider call yields one typed native joint observation. Its carrier may be a point set, region or field, ranked complete plans, posterior samples, structured chart, or another declared form. Resolution and calibration preserve that carrier and its dependence. Components may be factorized only when the provider contract and calibrated observation model establish the factorization. For a point-set carrier, the likelihood accounts for false positives, misses, location error, at-most-one-match, provider-family/repeated-call dependence, and over-segmentation; pointwise kernels are internal terms, never independent votes.
- In R4.8 use named joint-observation model, not set-level model.
- Title the table twelve cells and state that cells 1-11 plus 8b instantiate the point-set carrier without making it universal.
- Rename Q-A to Joint observation model; identify order-preserving assignment/detection as the point-set strawman.

RETURN 2 — R7 N3 makes a temporal edge endpoint a cell. Current source relations have RecallUnitId endpoints, while the new contract is specifically separating semantic artifacts from cells. A competing boundary plan does not by itself dissolve a semantic endpoint; this fixture reintroduces cell-as-semantic-object through the reject side.

Exact patch:
- Add the law: cells are never substituted for semantic or relation endpoints. A fixed-view projection that cannot preserve an endpoint artifact must publish typed loss/unresolved state rather than a dangling edge or silent deletion.
- Replace N3 with: a fixed-view projection includes a temporal relation but omits or cannot map one endpoint semantic artifact under the selected plan. Required disposition: refuse that fixed view or retain typed unresolved/loss; never publish the dangling relation.

These are the only blockers in my assigned segmentation/joint-uncertainty seat. Publish new exact bytes and I will re-review only these patches.
